subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What unit is used to measure the weight of paper and board?
questions.explain: Paper and board weight is measured in grams per square metre (gsm), with material over 200 gsm generally classed as board.

questions.q: Which board has a fluted, wavy inner layer that makes it ideal for protective packaging?
questions.explain: Corrugated card's fluted middle layer absorbs impact, making it strong yet lightweight for packaging.

questions.q: Why is layout paper well suited to producing quick design sketches?
options: It is thin and slightly translucent, so ideas can be traced and overlaid cheaply
It is rigid and thick, making it ideal for models
It is waterproof and hard-wearing for outdoor use
It has a glossy coating for photographic printing
questions.explain: Layout paper is thin, lightweight and translucent, allowing designers to trace over and refine sketches inexpensively.

questions.q: A designer needs primary packaging for a luxury perfume that requires a high-quality printed finish. Which material is most suitable?
questions.explain: Solid white board has a smooth, bleached surface that gives an excellent print finish for premium packaging.

questions.q: Why are hardwoods generally more expensive than softwoods?
options: They come from slow-growing deciduous trees that take many years to mature
They are made from recycled softwood chips
They must always be imported by air
They contain added metal to increase strength
questions.explain: Hardwoods come from slow-growing broadleaved (deciduous) trees, so their limited supply makes them costlier.

questions.q: Which of the following is a softwood?
questions.explain: Pine is a softwood from a coniferous tree, whereas oak, mahogany and beech are hardwoods.

questions.q: Why is MDF often chosen for painted furniture?
options: It has a smooth, grainless surface that is easy to finish
questions.explain: MDF is made from fine fibres and glue, giving a smooth, uniform surface with no grain that paints well.

questions.q: Why is plywood strong and resistant to warping?
options: Its veneers are glued together with the grain of each layer at 90 degrees to the next
It is cut from a single thick piece of hardwood
It contains a lightweight foam core
It is coated in a layer of metal
questions.explain: Cross-laminating veneers at right angles gives plywood strength in all directions and resists warping.

questions.q: Brass is an alloy of which two metals?
questions.explain: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc, valued for its corrosion resistance and attractive appearance.

questions.q: What do all ferrous metals contain?
questions.explain: Ferrous metals contain iron, which means most will rust and are magnetic.

questions.q: What is the key difference between thermoforming and thermosetting polymers?
options: Thermoforming polymers can be reheated and reshaped, while thermosetting polymers cannot once set
Thermosetting polymers can be recycled but thermoforming polymers cannot
Thermosetting polymers melt at lower temperatures
questions.explain: Thermoforming polymers soften and can be remoulded when heated, whereas thermosetting polymers set permanently.

questions.q: Which of the following is a natural fibre?
questions.explain: Cotton is a natural fibre grown from the cotton plant, while the others are synthetic fibres.

questions.q: Synthetic fibres such as polyester differ from natural fibres because they are...
options: Made from polymers derived from oil (petrochemicals)
questions.explain: Synthetic fibres are manufactured from petrochemical-based polymers rather than grown or harvested naturally.

questions.q: Which fabric is a non-woven material?
questions.explain: Felt is a non-woven fabric made by matting fibres together, unlike woven denim and calico or knitted jersey.

questions.q: A T-shirt maker wants a fabric that is comfortable and absorbent but also crease-resistant and hard-wearing. Which is the best choice?
questions.explain: Blending polyester with cotton combines cotton's comfort and absorbency with polyester's strength and crease resistance.

questions.q: Tensile strength is a material's ability to resist...
questions.explain: Tensile strength is the ability to withstand pulling or stretching forces without breaking.

questions.q: Which property allows a metal to be hammered or rolled into thin sheets without cracking?
questions.explain: Malleability is the ability to be permanently deformed by compression, such as rolling or pressing, without cracking.

questions.q: Ductility is best described as the ability of a material to be...
options: Drawn out into a thin wire
questions.explain: Ductility is the ability to be stretched or drawn into wires without breaking, as with copper.

questions.q: A support column in a structure must resist heavy squashing loads from above. Which property is most important?
questions.explain: Compressive strength is the ability to withstand squashing (compression) forces, essential for load-bearing columns.

questions.q: A designer is choosing a material for the cutting edge of a tool that must resist wear and scratching. Which property matters most?
questions.explain: Hardness is the ability to resist abrasion, wear and scratching, making it ideal for a durable cutting edge.
